TRIAGE DIRECTIVE (operator ruling 2026-10-03): this is an IMPLEMENTATION CHORE. Its specification and design are settled and accepted: openspec/changes/decision-0065-capabilities-slice-two/ (merged as 7f0aa4ad, council-cleared in run build-decision-0065-slice-two-co-50ef1e34) and decision 0077 (accepted). If the settled design cannot be implemented as written, the implement seat reports blocked; triage does not reopen the design.

BUILD DECISION 0065, SLICE TWO — UNIT U7d, one narrow visit, ONE pull request. Branch s2/U7d, cut from main at df112346. Recipe claude-flash-dsh-adv.

READ FIRST: design.md's "Slice two units" preamble and your unit (below, verbatim), the tasks your unit closes in tasks.md, the spec deltas it names, operator-ruling-2026-10-03.md, decision 0077 and decision 0065. Units before yours in your row's Dependencies have landed on main.

THE PREAMBLE, verbatim:
## Slice two units

One row is one PR, from main, signed and through the merge queue after the
operator rules. Follow this order. Dependencies are semantic prerequisites,
not simply the preceding row; the independence of U1–U4 is explicit in D9.
No row through U9a lifts the MCP compile fence. U9b is the sole enabling PR.
The lettered splits are required by the checked seams: record schema plus
embedded copy already consumes two files; multi-server wiring crosses runtime,
protocol and adapter data; storage/folding/inspect crosses CLI, protocol,
runtime and pure view. Minimal ledger writing is deliberately pulled into U6.

`contracts/realms.v<N>.schema.json` denotes one exact future file allocated
as **the next realms version after v7** at U5c, including v7's fields. It is
the only intentionally deferred filename number. Every other production path
below is literal. New paths are proposed modules/schemas, not files created
by this document plan. Constructors/registration are counted in their row.
Future tests extend the named suites; capability_broker already exists under
the consolidated CLI integration binary. New capability_artifacts and runtime
capability_ledger/capability_broker_launch modules are registered through the
existing test-only roots (CLI tests/it.rs and runtime tests/it.rs), not new
undeclared binaries. Tests may use child modules of the owning suites to stay
below 2,000 lines; list every test move in unit evidence.

Each row closes exactly its numbered tasks, including tests/mutations and
gate evidence. Test lists below are the allowed owning suites; every row
also updates this change's tasks and later implementation evidence. Measured
witness/compose pins accompany only rows that change their inputs.

YOUR ROW, verbatim:
| U7d | U7c | Deliver checked configurations and selected discovery; 36.1–37.2 | `crates/brokkr-protocol/src/adapters.rs`; `crates/brokkr-protocol/src/adapters/mcp.rs`; `crates/brokkr-protocol/src/native_controls/mcp.rs` |

YOUR UNIT, verbatim:
### U7d — Deliver checked configurations and selected discovery

Wire the expanded server set and dialect-secret environment removals into each U0-supported builder and final consumption point; unsupported measured carriers refuse. No modifications after checked command creation. Render fixed capability/tool discovery guidance from U7c's typed selected identifiers in the existing capability contract, reusing the measured hands.notice discovery identifier. No provider-name branch, new notice registry or parallel authority.

Configuration continues to carry only broker locator/digest, with no server values or direct bootstrap entry. Keep D5 box/clearance intent in the protected plan and remove every declared binding name from harness/broker inherited environments. The broker's independent pre-secret source/readiness check is still required after exact config proof; prompt discovery carries no mount/store facts.

Closes tasks 36.1, 36.2, 37.1 and 37.2; requirements [MB4](specs/mcp-capability-broker/spec.md), [MB1](specs/mcp-capability-broker/spec.md), [SI2](specs/strict-mcp-isolation/spec.md), [SD3](specs/slice-two-delivery/spec.md), [CC2](specs/capability-call-checkpoints/spec.md).
Proof: Actual composed cold/resume/replacement commands match independent literal server intent, and mutations refuse at the final serving boundary. Separately bind rendering and selection for Codex deferred discovery, fallback clearing, wanted drop and hostile prose; preserve hands notice, native/no-MCP prompts and requested-effect digest. No complete plan or storage locator reaches the renderer. Independently prove MB4's removal of exported dialect secret names from harness/broker environments, store-only child bindings and exact requires/wants authentication-collision causes at the serving boundary.

Operator rulings 2026-10-16, after the first run stopped blocked (0065-slice-two-unit-u7d-see-the--5977e175, no edits): U7d's row cannot make an engine-composed command carry brokers. The engine seals no brokered set (`isolation_intent` never yields `SealedServers::Brokered`), a single seat's serving inputs are sealed before its plans are provisioned, the plans' pins and dialect secret names never reach the sealed record, and no adapter declares its harness authentication names. U7d is split in three, run in order: U7d, U7d2, U7d3. U7d keeps its row and does the protocol half. Each U0-supported builder and the final serving check consume `SealedServers::Brokered` beside boxed hands; the Claude and LaneTally builders expand the set through `Servers::expand`; Codex and dsh, which have no measured broker carrier, refuse; the spawn removes each sealed removal from the harness environment and passes the same list as `Serving.removed`; group 37 parses the capability-server carrier once into a closed type and renders the fixed guidance in the existing capability contract. U7d proves this against hand-sealed serving inputs, as U7a did; the engine-composed cold, resume and replacement proof moves to U7d2 and the authentication-collision causes to U7d3. adapters.rs sits at its baseline, so new code goes in private child modules under the standing rule. No public API change is expected; any rise comes back to the operator at PR time. U7d closes tasks 37.1 and 37.2; tasks 36.1 and 36.2 close with U7d3.

Owning tests: `crates/brokkr-protocol/src/adapters/tests.rs`, `crates/brokkr-protocol/src/native_controls/tests.rs`, `crates/brokkr-runtime/src/engine/capability_tests.rs`, `crates/brokkr-runtime/src/engine/resume_tests.rs`, `crates/brokkr-runtime/tests/capability_launch.rs`.

CONTROLLER'S STATE FOR THIS RUN (the-forge-67, 2026-10-16). This is U7d's THIRD RUN.
- Run 1 (0065-slice-two-unit-u7d-see-the--5977e175) stopped blocked. The operator then split U7d into U7d, U7d2 and U7d3; prep has written that split into design.md and tasks.md in your worktree. Keep those amendments and do not reword them.
- Run 2 (0065-slice-two-unit-u7d-see-the--dc274405) built the protocol half as signed commit fdd8102c and passed verify. Review then stopped it with REVIEW-SECURITY-HOLD. YOUR WORKTREE ARRIVES WITH THAT WORK STAGED: prep replayed fdd8102c onto main, leaving out quality/file-lines.txt (regenerate the rows you move), tasks.md (re-tick 37.1 and 37.2 on evidence) and adapters/capability_calls.rs (see L1). KEEP the replay. Fix the two findings below, rerun every gate, and commit signed.

H1 HIGH SECURITY (review chief, reproduced): the dialect secret names reach the harness's --version probe.
- In adapters/mcp.rs (about :108, :114, :239), the thread-local REMOVED starts empty. It receives the current sealed names only after served() succeeds.
- But adapters.rs (about :3660 and :3678) calls qualify before served_plan. observed_version (about :1238) calls run_cli → spawn_harness (about :735), whose unbind then uses an empty list or the previous attempt's.
- So a first cold launch with an enabled resume assessment, or a qualified rejoin, exposes an exported dialect credential to the harness's --version process before the final model command is checked.
- The chief reproduced it through target/debug/brokkr's `driver claude`: a valid hand-sealed Brokered configuration, a supported boxed-workspace assessment, and a temporary synthetic harness that prints whether a synthetic exported U7D_REVIEW_DIALECT_TOKEN is in its environment. The output was 'probe:present' then 'model:absent'.
- MB4 and decision 0077 ruling 3 require those names to be absent from EVERY harness process of the attempt.
- Fix: carry the current attempt's removals, taken from its sealed serving input, explicitly to every harness spawn of that attempt, qualification and version probes included. Never rely on an earlier served() call, and never let one attempt's list outlive it. Prefer an explicit value over ambient thread state. Where adapters.rs's baseline leaves no room, move code into a private child module under the standing rule.
- Bind with compiling removals:
  (a) a first cold launch with a resume assessment: probe absent, model absent;
  (b) a qualified rejoin: same;
  (c) two attempts with different removal lists: each spawn removes exactly its own attempt's names, and nothing carries over;
  (d) an attempt with no brokers removes nothing extra.
  A test like the chief's synthetic-harness probe is the model. Use no real credential or provider.

L1 LOW (scope): adapters/capability_calls.rs is declared `pub mod` from adapters.rs, so the standing exception for EXISTING PRIVATE child modules does not cover it. Prep left it out, so it is unchanged from main. In discovery.rs, replace the `capability_calls::mcp_tool` import by spelling `mcp__<server>__<tool>` there, with a comment naming capability_calls.rs's MCP_PREFIX/MCP_SEPARATOR as the other home. Add a test that the name discovery renders equals the name a capability_calls Observation shows for the same server and tool, so the two homes cannot drift. Correct evidence/U7d.md's scope claim: it touches the three row files, the new private child adapters/discovery.rs, and test files.

Update evidence/U7d.md: add a section for this run naming H1, the fix, its four bindings and the chief's reproduction redone on your head (probe absent, model absent), plus L1.

CONTROLLER NOTE (from the-forge-45, 2026-10-13): #434 slice 1 reshaped parts of crates/brokkr-protocol/src/adapters.rs before this unit. If it has landed on main, read it before you edit:
- Every invoke_* exit-code read (invoke_stream_json, invoke_codex, invoke_dsh, invoke_dsh_stream_json, invoke_with_stager) goes through ONE reader in adapters/lost.rs, where a signal is SIGNALLED, never -1. Don't reintroduce `status.code().unwrap_or(-1)`.
- spawn_harness records "spawned" for the attempt via a thread_local in adapters/lost.rs. Codex cold replacement in invoke_with_stager reads lost::exited_non_zero.
- run_seat / run_seat_with keep a fixed ending order. A refusal returns only via lost::refusal_to_start. The unsettled arm and the by_signal arm send no result, and a signal is checked ahead of the dialect arm. serve_io ends when a start sent no result. Keep that order when you edit run_seat_with's tail.
- adapters/lost.rs is an existing private child of your row file adapters.rs; the child-module rule lets you change it.
- CARRIED LOW (U6f1a's re-vouch review, 2026-10-13, decision 0071 ruling 5): crates/brokkr-protocol/src/adapters.rs about :710 repeats "mask, then lossy-decode" by hand, when secret::mask_text (public since U6f1a) does exactly that. adapters.rs is your row file: call secret::mask_text there, and bind the change with a regression and a removal.

CARRIED TEST FIX (controller, 2026-10-16; reported by the-forge-45, test files are not bounded by the row): crates/brokkr-cli/tests/capability_broker/observer.rs `the_admitted_launcher_runs_through_its_handle_with_no_environment` (assertion at about :854) flakes under load. It failed in 2 of 3 host exact-coverage runs on an unrelated branch, because strace logged one extra line after the execve, `???()                           = ?`. That is strace's marker for an unfinished call of a tracee that died mid-call. Drop lines whose call starts with `???(` before the comparison, with a comment saying why. Keep the exact single-execve assertion. Bind it with a compiling removal: drop the filter and feed a recorded log that holds the marker line, through a small helper over the log text if that makes it testable. Record it in your evidence file.

STANDING RULINGS. Decision 0065's hold: off by default, no grandfathering; realm-only grants; tools are an abstraction, dialects the concrete; refuse, never reconcile (slice one's operator ruling of 2026-09-23). The MCP compile fence stays in place until U9b. Hosts are Linux and macOS only (decision 0063). Main's code-health rules bind: no `unsafe` in brokkr-runtime; `#[expect(.., reason)]`, never `#[allow]`; clippy's too_many_lines, excessive_nesting and struct_excessive_bools are denied, so split, and only if splitting would widen your unit carry `reason = "baseline 2026-09-29, decision 0065 slice one merged with main; split after #319"`; when a count moves, re-measure quality/'s file-lines, too-many-lines and suppressions (the steps quality/measure.sh uses), witness pins with `BROKKR_BLESS=1 cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --test witness_digests` (or, once #423's single test binary is on your base — crates/brokkr-runtime/tests/it.rs exists — `BROKKR_BLESS=1 cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --test it witness_digests::`), and budgets with scripts/measure-budgets.sh. Where a crate has tests/it.rs, a NEW tests/*.rs file must be registered as `mod <file>;` in that crate's tests/it.rs (layering::test_targets refuses an unregistered one), unless it sets HOME, cwd, env or a global allocator, in which case it is its own [[test]] in Cargo.toml with the reason written there; and `--test <file>` filters become `--test it <file>::` (capability_launch stays its own binary).

RULES. Touch at most the production files your row names; if the real scope exceeds them, STOP and report `oversized` with the split. One exception, the operator's standing rule of 2026-10-09 (operator-ruling-2026-10-03.md): beside a production file in your row that sits at its 800-line ceiling, or is frozen at its quality/file-lines.txt baseline above it, you may add NEW private child modules, declared from that file, in its own module tree and consumed in this unit, without stopping. The same holds beside a row file that your own change would push past 800 lines (extended 2026-10-11). You may also change an EXISTING private child module of a file in your row, in that file's own module tree (extended 2026-10-11). You may move existing code out of the full file into such a child to make room, preferring the code your change touches. Name each new file in your evidence and commit, and set its quality/file-lines.txt row. You may also add a name to an EXISTING re-export in the parent module that declares one of your row's files, where the parent's line count does not change (extended 2026-10-10). Files in any other module tree still mean `oversized`; any public API growth still needs the operator's ruling at PR time (record it, do not stop). Test files are NOT bounded by the row (controller's standing clarification, 2026-10-05): a test anywhere that pins behaviour your unit changes, a validator or fixture swap in another suite, or a new child test module beside an owning suite that sits over its line ceiling is part of your unit — size-neutral wherever a file sits at its quality/file-lines.txt baseline. A LOW finding you cannot fix inside your row's production files: record it in your result and do NOT report blocked for it. Tests assert exact reasons and values, never is_err(); every new test is bound by a compiling mutation that makes it fail, then restored, recorded (test, assertion) in evidence.md. Tick a task in tasks.md only on observed evidence; record results in a NEW file of your own, openspec/changes/decision-0065-capabilities-slice-two/evidence/U7d.md (two lanes deliver units at once, and every unit appending to evidence.md made each pair of pull requests conflict), and do not edit evidence.md itself; write it in prose or a table — never as a bullet list of the standard gate lines (`cargo fmt ...: clean`, `cargo clippy ...: clean`), which earlier evidence files already hold word for word, so the data clone gate refuses it; never edit the tasks.md preamble. Fixtures build on a canonicalised temporary root; no test reads .forge/ or needs an installed provider. Frozen contracts, policy/phase-machine.json, fixtures/, reference/ and extensions/ do not move unless your unit names them. Sign every commit (`git commit -S`; main requires signatures). HEADLESS SEAT: your session ends the moment you end a turn — never run a command in the background, never use Monitor or ScheduleWakeup, run every command in the foreground under the tool's 10-minute limit (suites crate by crate with `timeout 590`, split by --lib/--test if longer), and write your result file before you finish. GATES: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings; the suite of each crate you touched; openspec validate --all --strict; typos --hidden; git diff --check; quality/ratchet.sh files and clones. CI also builds and tests on macOS, which this host cannot: Linux-only code (namespaces, mountinfo, /proc, device numbers, Linux-only syscalls) goes behind `#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]` with a non-Linux stand-in that refuses, as broker/session.rs does, and any libc or rustix type you use must be the same type on both (rustix's Dev is u64 on Linux and i32 on macOS; U6c6a's first PR failed to compile there). Keep the session small; commit when the unit is done; never push.

instructions.analyze:
# OpenSpec analyze

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.
instructions.clarify:
# OpenSpec clarify

Judge underspecified areas, unquantified language, missing decisions, capability/delta mismatches, and requirements without adequate scenarios. Return every ambiguity with the evidence needed to settle it; zero findings is clear.
instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.
instructions.implement:
# OpenSpec tasks

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/tasks.md` as numbered groups of checkboxes. Name the requirement served by every task. On return, repair the breakdown and its requirement coverage before implementation resumes.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.
instructions.review:
# OpenSpec specify

Create or adopt `openspec/changes/<change>/proposal.md`, then write the capability deltas under `specs/`. The proposal keeps `Why`, `What Changes`, and `Capabilities`; each delta uses requirements and scenarios. On return, answer every finding in the artifacts and keep the proposal and deltas coherent.

# OpenSpec design

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `recipes/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.
